statusText: Eight of the twenty-four published hours fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt and no United States macro release lands anywhere in the window, holding Tail at the closed-venue floor. Every Friday primary mark was re-verified unchanged this run. The two verified weekend threads point in opposite directions: a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted at dawn on Saturday with no reported casualties or damage, while crude closed Friday lower for a third consecutive session as Aramco prepared a partial restart of the East-West pipeline.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail of 5 sits far below the 25% block threshold and no danger window is identified, because the current hour falls inside the weekend futures halt and no live NQ price path exists to assess. The 22:00Z restart is published at Tail 18, the window high and still inside the EA_ON band. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: An intercepted Riyadh missile and a third straight lower close in crude leave the weekend ledger two-sided: the venue stays halted for eight of the 24 published hours and the 22:00Z restart carries the window's only elevated allowance
body:
Eight of the 24 hours published here fall inside the CME equity-futures weekend halt. The remaining sixteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session that follows and the European hours into Monday morning. Cash equities last traded on Friday 18 September and there has been no live NQ price path since 21:00Z that day.

Every Friday mark was re-verified at primary sources for this run and all are unchanged. The Nasdaq-100 settled 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% against a previous close of 29,447.00, finishing 3.63 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range and about 3.6% below its 30,762.20 annual high. VIX closed 14.81, down 4.08%, near the low end of a 13.38-35.30 annual range. The H.15 release for 17 September prints the 2-year at 4.67%, the 10-year at 4.94% and the effective federal funds rate at 3.88%, the last confirming the 25 basis point hike delivered the previous week. WTI is marked at 100.30 dollars, down 1.58%, with Brent at 103.87.

The session itself was rotational rather than directional. The Nasdaq Composite added 0.4% and the S&P 500 0.2% while the Dow slipped 0.2%, and reporting attributed the split to a 10-year yield hovering near 5% against a semiconductor complex that recovered through the afternoon. Latest-session cross-asset context, which is delayed and not a live price path, showed the same shape: semiconductor names broadly higher with software lower, and megacaps split four up and four down around a mean near a quarter of a percent. That is conflict, which belongs in Stress and Confidence, not one-way structure of the kind that would lift Tail.

Two weekend threads meet the restart. Saudi air defences intercepted a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh at dawn on Saturday, the first such attempt on the capital since the July escalation, with further attempts on Bisha, Taif, Farasan and Yanbu reported as thwarted and no casualties or damage confirmed. Against that, the East-West pipeline that normally carries 4-5% of global oil supply has been shut since 11 September and Aramco has been reported preparing a partial restart, which is the supply-relief thread behind three consecutive lower closes in crude. Because the two point in opposite directions, the restart is published as a wider two-sided distribution rather than as a directional gap.

No danger window is set. A narrow window requires evidence, and no open venue has produced any since Friday. The published path instead carries a graduated conditional allowance that peaks at Tail 18 at the 22:00Z restart and decays through a thin Asian session with Tokyo closed for Respect for the Aged Day. Every one of the 24 hours maps to EA_ON.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green with dominant mode normal, because no venue was open to produce classifiable structure at any point in the window. Tail held 5 through the first eight slots, eased to 4 from 22:00Z Saturday through 04:00Z Sunday and returned to 5 across the final nine slots. Stress opened at 22, drifted through 23 and 24 across Saturday evening, stepped to 26 after midnight, eased to 25, then jumped to 29 at 05:00Z as the weekend escalation reporting landed and settled between 28 and 31 through the Sunday hours. Confidence ranged from 72 to 76 with no slot outside that band, reflecting a research record that stayed complete while the live-structure gap stayed open throughout.
outlookSummary: Eight of the 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt; the remaining sixteen contain the 22:00Z restart, the Asian session and the European hours into Monday morning. No United States macro release falls anywhere inside this window, the only scheduled US catalysts in it are the Goolsbee speech at 10:30Z and the Chicago Fed National Activity Index at 12:30Z on Monday, and the first high-impact print is Wednesday's flash PMIs. Tail holds 5 for the current hour, steps gradually to 14 across the remaining halt hours and peaks at the window high of 18 at the restart, where a thin Sunday-evening book meets an unpriced weekend headline set, then decays through an Asian session with Tokyo shut for a public holiday and settles between 10 and 12 across the European hours. Every slot maps to EA_ON because no observed one-way structure exists anywhere in the verified record, and the published steps are conditional allowances rather than claims about price action that has not happened.

forecast.analysis: Mid-afternoon halt hour. European and US cash desks are closed and no macro release falls anywhere in this part of the window, so elapsed time is the only moving part. Confidence eases roughly a point an hour as the verified Friday marks age; the conditional risk path remains two-sided.
drivers: No US or European macro release falls inside the weekend halt
Confidence eases as Friday's verified marks age hour by hour

forecast.analysis: Four hours to the restart. Stress ticks up because the two weekend threads that will meet the reopening pull in opposite directions: a ballistic missile aimed at Riyadh was intercepted on Saturday, while Aramco is preparing a partial pipeline restart. Neither has been priced by any open venue.

Aramco preparing a partial East-West restart; full capacity guided at weeks
A two-sided weekend thread raises Stress rather than Tail

forecast.analysis: Three hours out, Tail reaches double digits as a conditional allowance for the thin Sunday-evening tape that follows any halt. This is an allowance for a wider opening distribution, not an observation: no pullback depth, extension behaviour or session extreme can be measured while the venue is shut.
drivers: Sunday-evening restart tape is structurally thin; wider opening distribution
No pullback depth or extension behaviour is measurable inside the halt
Reported early return of the US president from Camp David on Saturday

forecast.analysis: Two hours out and the allowance widens again into the restart. The checkpoint for the hours that follow is whether the first prints hold a one-way path or retrace. Only an observed refusal to retrace would justify Tail above the watch band, and nothing in the verified record supports that yet.
drivers: Checkpoint: do the first restart prints retrace or extend one-way
Only an observed refusal to retrace would justify Tail above the watch band

forecast.analysis: Final halt hour and the pre-open high of this window. Stress reflects the stack that meets the reopening: Saudi supply offline, a 10-year near 5%, and a Fed that hiked for the first time since 2023 with one further move penciled in for 2026. Tail stays well inside the EA_ON band.
drivers: Last hour before the 22:00Z CME equity-futures restart
Catalyst stack: Saudi supply outage, 10Y near 5%, Fed in hiking mode
Futures reported near 42% odds of two further 2026 hikes

forecast.analysis: First full hour of live discovery. Tail eases from the restart high on the assumption that the opening repricing is absorbed. If early prints instead extend without retracing, that assumption is invalidated and this published level would understate the risk. None of it is observed at the time of writing.
drivers: First full hour of live NQ discovery after the weekend halt
Published decay assumes the opening repricing is absorbed
Invalidation: early extension with no retracement breaks that assumption

forecast.analysis: The Asian session begins with Tokyo shut for Respect for the Aged Day, thinning the regional bid and the usual cross-check on overnight direction. Published Tail continues to decay on the assumption of orderly two-way discovery; the thinner book is why that decay is gradual rather than immediate.
drivers: Tokyo closed Monday for Respect for the Aged Day; thinner Asian liquidity
Decay assumes orderly two-way discovery rather than one-way extension
No US macro release falls anywhere in the Asian hours

forecast.analysis: Second Asian hour. With Japan out, Hong Kong and Sydney carry the session and index futures more often range than trend in that configuration. The published step down reflects that base rate and the absence of any scheduled catalyst, not an observation about how the restart actually resolved.
drivers: Hong Kong and Sydney carry the session with Japan closed
No scheduled catalyst falls inside the hour
Step reflects a thin-session base rate, not an observed outcome

forecast.analysis: Mid-Asian hour. A restart that repriced cleanly would by now show decaying realised volatility and two-way rotation, which is exactly the condition the published decay assumes. It is a checkpoint rather than a claim: the same hour would carry materially higher risk under a persistent one-way path.
drivers: Checkpoint: decaying realised volatility and two-way rotation by mid-Asia
The published decay is conditional on that checkpoint being met
Crude and Treasury futures remain the key cross-asset confirmation

forecast.analysis: Late Asian hour into the European handover, with Tail approaching this window's floor for open-venue hours. The weekend escalation thread stays in Stress rather than Tail because an interception without casualties or damage is headline risk, not a demonstrated failure of mean reversion.
drivers: Late Asian hour ahead of the European handover
Interception without damage is headline risk, not demonstrated path failure
Escalation stays a Stress input rather than a Tail amplifier

news.title: Saudi Arabia says air defences intercepted Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh

forecast.analysis: Quiet pre-European hour. No scheduled US or euro-area release lands here and the Asian book thins ahead of the handover. The published scores flatten, which is the appropriate shape when neither a catalyst nor an observed structural change is available to justify moving them.
drivers: No scheduled US or euro-area release inside the hour
Asian book thinning ahead of the European handover
Flat path where no catalyst or observed change justifies movement

forecast.analysis: European pre-market. Confidence begins recovering because by this hour a live overnight price path exists to assess, closing the evidence gap that caps every weekend reading. Tail sits at the open-venue floor of this window in the absence of any observed extension.
drivers: Confidence recovers as a live overnight price path becomes assessable
Tail at this window's open-venue floor absent observed extension
European pre-market flow builds ahead of the 07:00Z cash open

forecast.analysis: Final hour before European cash trade. The overnight range established since the restart becomes the session reference, and a contained range would confirm the published decay. A range that instead marked repeated new extremes without retracement would argue for a materially higher reading.
drivers: Overnight range since the restart becomes the European session reference
A contained range would confirm the published decay
Repeated new extremes without retracement would argue for a higher reading

forecast.analysis: European cash open. Frankfurt and London add real volume for the first time since Friday, and session-transition hours carry a modest structural allowance for a directional impulse. The step is deliberately small because no observed evidence of one-way behaviour exists in the verified record.

Session-transition hours carry a modest directional-impulse allowance

forecast.analysis: First full European hour. Semiconductor and megacap tone is the cross-check that matters most for the Nasdaq-100 here. Friday's latest-session context showed semis leading and software lagging, which is rotational rather than one-way, and treating it as live Monday structure would overstate the case.

forecast.analysis: Mid-European hour with no scheduled US catalyst, leaving crude as the cross-asset to watch. A confirmed partial restart of the East-West pipeline would extend the supply-relief impulse, while a fresh strike on Saudi infrastructure would reverse it. Either outcome resolves into Stress before it reaches Tail.

forecast.analysis: The hour after the scheduled speech. A hawkish reading would most plausibly transmit through the front end, and a 2-year at 4.67% against a 10-year at 4.94% leaves a thin cushion for further curve compression. That is a Stress channel; it becomes a Tail question only if equities then refuse to retrace.

forecast.analysis: The Chicago Fed National Activity Index for August is scheduled at 12:30Z. It is a second-tier print that rarely sets index direction on its own, and it lands in the pre-open hour when positioning rather than data usually drives the tape. Published scores stay close to flat across this stretch.

Stress reaches the window high as the week's agenda comes into view: flash PMIs Wednesday, jobless claims Thursday and a Washington summit on the 24th with AI and trade on the agenda. Tail stays inside the EA_ON band throughout.
